findings.title: DreamHost Urges Affected Customers to Reset All Email and FTP Passwords
findings.summary_md: DreamHost's web-based File Manager has been unavailable since October 23, 2026. During the outage the company expired passwords for some email and FTP/SFTP users as a precaution, and affected users cannot sign in until the account owner sets a replacement password. DreamHost asked account owners to check each mailbox for unfamiliar forwarding rules and warned that it will never email users asking for passwords. The company said it was still investigating the cause and had not confirmed that credentials were accessed.

findings.title: DreamHost forces password resets in ongoing "incident"
findings.summary_md: DreamHost forced password resets for email and FTP/SFTP users after an incident disrupted connections to the File Manager interface. The provider initially reported File Manager connectivity problems on October 23, 2026, then blocked access until users completed resets. As of publication the incident remained active and File Manager access was still unavailable. BleepingComputer said DreamHost had not responded to questions about the number of impacted accounts or whether files or messages were exposed.

findings.title: DreamHost Security Incident Forces Password Resets for Email and FTP/SFTP Accounts
findings.summary_md: DreamHost implemented forced password resets for certain email and FTP/SFTP accounts after an incident affected its File Manager and webmail services. The company restored its browser-based File Manager on October 26, 2026, but affected users still need new credentials from their account owners. The disruption began October 23 with File Manager connectivity issues, followed by precautionary resets for webmail and FTP/SFTP. The updates did not identify the root cause, disclose affected account counts, or confirm unauthorized access or data theft.

findings.title: DreamHost incident triggers password resets, locks customers out of email and FTP accounts
findings.summary_md: DreamHost brought its File Manager back online after an incident that disrupted several services, though some customers remained locked out of email or FTP accounts until passwords were reset. The first sign of trouble came on the afternoon of October 23, 2026, when connectivity problems hit the File Manager interface. DreamHost described the resets as precautionary and said affected users cannot sign in until the account owner resets their passwords. The company said all affected account owners had been emailed instructions by October 25.

findings.title: Unexplained DreamHost Incident Prompts Email, FTP Password Resets
findings.summary_md: Over the weekend of October 25-26, 2026, DreamHost suspended its File Manager service and reset some user passwords. The company said it took protective actions in response to an issue affecting File Manager at files.dreamhost.com and DreamHost webmail. DreamHost told account owners that users would need new passwords when logging in and that it would not request password resets by email. DreamHost later created and deployed a fix and restored access to files.dreamhost.com while monitoring stability.

findings.title: October Security Incident
findings.summary_md: DreamHost disclosed that an unauthorized third party accessed the server running its web-based File Manager at files.dreamhost.com, discovered on the afternoon of October 23, 2026. The intruder exploited a vulnerability in the File Manager software and could access FTP/SFTP usernames and passwords of users who logged in between approximately August 2026 and October 23, 2026. DreamHost said the attacker may also have accessed webmail systems, exposing session information including credentials for a limited number of users. The company said it found no evidence of control panel login or billing data exposure, and that the affected group was well under approximately 10 percent of hosted email and FTP/SFTP accounts.
